newsitem.title: CHINA: Chinese negotiator invited to visit rival Taiwan.
newsitem.headline: Chinese negotiator invited to visit rival Taiwan.

text.p: China and Taiwan on Tuesday agreed to step up cooperation on crime fighting, and one of Beijing's top negotiators with Taipei was invited to visit the rival island in a sign of thawing ties, sources said.

Lee Ching-ping, deputy secretary-general of Taiwan's Straits Exchange Foundation who is visiting China, invited his Chinese counterpart, Liu Gangqi, to visit the island, said the sources close to Lee's delegation.
The invitation was extended during a meeting between Lee and China's top negotiator with Taiwan, Tang Shubei, in Beijing on Tuesday. There was no timetable for Liu to visit the island.
The quasi-official foundation handles Taiwan's ties with China in the absence of formal ties.

Taiwan's Nationalists, who lost the Chinese civil war to the Communists in 1949, still ban official contacts with the mainland, notwithstanding a thaw in the 1980s that allowed semi-official talks to take place.
Talks between the two sides have been suspended since mid-1995 after Taiwan's President Lee Teng-hui made a private but high-profile visit to the United States.

China, which regards Taiwan as a renegade province, was enraged by Lee's U.S. trip, suspecting it was an attempt to promote independence for Taiwan rather than reunification with the mainland. Taiwan denies the charge.

The Chinese military conducted war games and missiles tests near Taiwan in March 1996 to intimidate the island in the run-up to its first direct presidential elections. President Lee was re-elected by a landslide.
Lee, the Taiwanese negotiator, also met Chinese Justice Ministry officials and the two sides agreed to step up cooperation on crime fighting and the repatriation of fugitives, the sources said.
Lee arrived in Beijing on Monday for a five-day visit. The two Lees are not related.
Taiwan has repeatedly urged China to resume semi-official talks to resolve issues facing both sides -- including fishing disputes, repatriation of airline hijackers and stowaways.
